name: Rule of thumb for matching fly size to tippet
q: Rule of thumb for matching fly size to tippet
a: Divide hook size by 3 (or 4 for a stealthier presentation) → X. Size 12 fly ÷ 3 = 4X.

name: What does the X number mean?
q: What does the X number mean?
a: Diameter: X = (11 − diameter in thousandths). 4X = .007 in. Higher X = thinner.

name: Tapered leader anatomy
q: Tapered leader anatomy
a: ~60% butt (stiff, turns over), ~20% taper (steps down), ~20% tippet (level, replaceable).

name: Standard trout leader
q: Standard trout leader
a: 9 ft 4X or 5X. Go 12 ft for spooky spring-creek fish; 7.5 ft for streamers or small brushy water.

name: Streamer leader
q: Streamer leader
a: Short and stout: 4-7.5 ft of 0X-2X (10-15 lb). On a sink tip, 3-4 ft level.

name: Dry-dropper spacing
q: Dry-dropper spacing
a: Dropper tippet 12-36 in below the dry, tied to the hook bend; depth ≈ 1.5× water depth for nymphs under an indicator.

name: Euro nymph leader
q: Euro nymph leader
a: Long thin level mono (~20 ft), colored sighter section, 4-6 ft tippet; heavy point fly, lighter dropper above.

name: Bonefish leader
q: Bonefish leader
a: 9-12 ft tapering to 10-12 lb fluoro tippet (flats fluoro sinks and is abrasion-resistant).

name: Permit leader
q: Permit leader

name: Tarpon leader
q: Tarpon leader
a: Butt → Bimini class tippet (16-20 lb) → 40-80 lb fluoro shock/bite tippet, ~12-18 in.

name: Striped bass / bluefish leader
q: Striped bass / bluefish leader
a: 6-9 ft of 20-30 lb; add wire or 50-60 lb bite for bluefish.

name: Barracuda / needlefish leader
q: Barracuda / needlefish leader
a: Wire bite tippet (knottable wire, ~30 lb) joined with Albright.

name: Fluoro vs nylon
q: Fluoro vs nylon
a: Fluoro: sinks, less visible, abrasion-resistant — nymphs, streamers, salt. Nylon: floats, cheaper, more stretch — dries.

name: Fly line taper: WF vs DT
q: Fly line taper: WF vs DT
a: Weight-forward loads fast and shoots line — default. Double taper for delicate short casts and roll casts.

name: Sink rates
q: Sink rates
a: Floating → intermediate (1-2 ips) → sink tip (type 3-6) → full sink. Choose by depth and current speed.

name: Backing amounts
q: Backing amounts
a: Trout: 75-100 yd 20 lb. Salt 8-10wt: 200+ yd 30 lb. Tarpon: 300 yd 30-50 lb or gel-spun.
